title: Ford 4.9L · engine atlas
status: In-progress reconstruction; not a complete or verified OEM engine

definitions.name: Piston
definitions.function: Receives combustion force at the crown and transfers it through the wrist pin. D-shaped dish, underside and ring grooves are modeled; skirt profile and pin offset remain provisional.
unresolved: Inherited piston-study assumptions; exact forging, ring profiles, pin offset and fastener threads remain unresolved.

definitions.name: Wrist pin
definitions.function: Connects piston and rod at their small-end joint. Retainer configuration and offset need confirmation.
unresolved: Inherited piston-study assumptions; exact forging, ring profiles, pin offset and fastener threads remain unresolved.

definitions.name: Top compression ring
definitions.function: Seals combustion gases and transfers heat toward the bore. Individual split ring; exact section profile is not yet reconstructed.

definitions.name: Connecting rod

definitions.name: Oil filter steel case
definitions.function: Contains the pressurized filter assembly. Shallow removal flutes are illustrative; the shell uses a WIX comparison envelope.
unresolved: This is a construction study, not a verified FL-1A or WIX51515 internal replica. The 93mm diameter/132mm overall envelope and72/63/5mm gasket use WIX published metric comparison dimensions; the truck factory specifies FL-1A.
Pleat count, wall thicknesses, internal seats, valve parts and spring geometry are illustrative. No oil flow, filtering efficiency, bypass pressure or seal compression is simulated.
The insert is a hollow stepped comparison envelope, not a reconstructed E4TZ-6890-A anti-drainback service insert. No unsourced valve mechanism is added.

Filter position, inclined boss, gallery routing, insert lengths, block-end thread diameter and sealing lands are provisional. Filter-side 3/4-16 uses coincident nominal male/female envelopes, not helical thread contact.

Two deliberately open side interfaces bound this gallery study. They are not production external ports and remain disconnected from the pump and main oil gallery. The engine lubrication circuit is incomplete.

No separate adapter gasket or additional bypass valve is inferred. The existing filter gasket, internal flap and illustrative bypass remain separate components; seal compression and anti-drainback performance are not simulated.

definitions.name: Oil filter baseplate
definitions.function: Outer inlet holes communicate with the boss inlet annulus; the central threaded-envelope bore receives the hollow mounting insert. Complete pump/main-gallery routing and actual thread contact remain unresolved.

definitions.name: FS10 Rear Cylinder
definitions.function: One cylinder/case half guides five piston ends, surrounds the swash chamber and reacts bearing loads. The front half includes provisional bracket ears; two provisional longitudinal galleries connect the head plenums. A nominal stepped bore seats the separate unresolved radial shaft-bearing cartridge; bearing dimensions and housing fits remain provisional.
unresolved: DENSO identifies FS10 471-8130 for the 1990–95 F-150 4.9 factory-A/C branch. Owner photos show A/C, but installed identity and factory/dealer branch are unresolved.

Five double-ended pistons, ten shoes, swashplate/shaft, two cylinder halves and valve/reed stacks follow Ford FS10 architecture and a 1998 Crown Victoria dissection. This is not truck-specific teardown evidence.

UAC CO101220C supplies a 145 mm clutch diameter and six grooves for 1990–95 F-series 4.9. Diameter is used as an outside envelope, not a verified belt pitch diameter. Its 93 mm tangent mount width lacks a diagrammed datum and is not yet applied. Case diameter, cylinder pitch/bore, 18 degree swash angle, groove profile, axial lengths, mount ears and manifold ports remain provisional.
Clutch static gap is 0.6 mm, within the Ford 1994 specification 0.4572–0.8382 mm. Friction, electromagnetics, refrigerant, oil and thermodynamics are not simulated.
Piston displacement and shoe face orientation are analytic swashplate relationships; checked discrete poses do not prove production motion, pressure sealing or continuous clearance.
Thrust rolling elements and pulley bearing are envelope cartridges, not counted rollers. Reed flexure, shaft splines, seals, fastener threads, piston coatings and manufacturing fits are simplified.
Mount ears at X432.56, Y210/350, Z60/140 and the X473.56 belt center are shared provisional accessory-bracket interfaces, not measured truck locations. Vehicle refrigerant lines are omitted.

Ford describes gas-tight passages through the cylinder connecting both heads to rear suction/discharge ports. The two 4 mm longitudinal galleries, radial head-cap drillings, concentric plenums and full reed sheets are an illustrative connected topology, not traced production passages.
Two fixed spherical sockets per piston allow rigid piston translation and shoe rotation without geometry morphing. The socket spacing and 18 degree swash inclination remain provisional.

Independent compressor angle and engagement controls are not coupled to crank angle or a claimed belt pitch ratio. Engagement gates motion only; this simplified combined hub/armature does not flex or close its static gap.

Disengagement resets the mechanism to its reference pose; it does not simulate physical run-down. Shared illustrative PK groove normalization uses 3.56 mm pitch and 40 degree flanks, not a traced Ford pulley section.

Open-channel probes and seated-reed obstruction checks establish selected geometric routes, not a pressure-tight fluid simulation. Piston-ring clearances, oil films, reed lift and leakage are not solved.

Summit FS10 illustration identifies one shaft bearing in each cylinder half, distinct from the adjacent thrust stack. This establishes the comparison support count, not the installed truck bearing identity.

The 20 mm bore, 28 mm outside diameter, 12 mm width and axial stations at plus/minus 42 mm are assumed to match the existing study shaft and cylinder envelope. No catalog bearing number or production fit is asserted.
Each radial bearing is one unresolved cartridge envelope. Rolling elements, cage, cup, raceways, lubrication details and manufacturing tolerances are not reconstructed or counted.
Matched nominal shaft and housing contact surfaces describe a load-path interface only. Zero-clearance CAD contact is not a press-fit, running-clearance, wear or bearing-load calculation.

Provisional isolated longitudinal galleries connect both heads. Rear port lands and a blind retaining-bolt socket accommodate the separate provisional manifold and two size 211 comparison seals. The manifold-boss revision retains the original cap drillings and a separate blind bolt socket; all dimensions remain illustrative.

Two rear-facing port seals follow the UAC CO101220C application photo and Summit FS10 construction illustration. Summit lists 211C70 suction/discharge seals; its size table supplies the nominal .796 inch bore and .139 inch section. Installed seal identity remains unverified.

Rear-head pads, manifold contour, port pitch, passage bore, axial stations and bolt geometry remain provisional. The original study port axes are retained; no photograph is treated as a dimensional drawing.
Nominal undeformed toroidal seals sit in matching illustrative two-sided seats. This is not a production gland, seal squeeze, pressure rating or leak-tightness calculation.
The single fastener follows the 1994 factory manifold-bolt description. Its diameter, length and head are assumed; threads, engagement and clamp loads are not reconstructed.
The manifold contains two separate open through passages. Vehicle refrigerant tubes, hose crimps and complete installed routing are absent; no shipping plate is included as an operating component.

Original provisional suction/discharge cap drillings are restored through the added manifold mounting boss. This preserves the complete accepted diagnostic flow paths, not just the two external port probes.

The manifold retaining-bolt socket is blind at local axial station -86 mm, leaving an illustrative 2 mm wall to the nearest suction cap drilling. Thread engagement, pressure wall adequacy and production geometry remain unverified.

unresolved: Factory PMGR architecture/counts and manual F2TZ11002ARM identity are supported; J&N replacement cross-reference supplies ten pinion teeth,27.7mm OD and11mm mounting-hole diameter. Remaining dimensions are provisional.
Starter center distance, clocking, axial station,12mm travel and housing envelope are fit-study assumptions. No bellhousing, index-plate bore or mounting bolt support is reconstructed or claimed.

The9.525mm ring-face setback is a manual164-tooth Ford V8 comparison, not a verified4.9L mounting datum. Existing flywheel tooth module/pressure angle are also assumptions; sampled mesh is not production certification.

Internal12/18/48 tooth reducer counts,5:1 ratio, winding/commutator subdivision and clearances are assumptions. Electromagnetics, current, insulation performance, overrunning-clutch internals and solenoid contact switching are not simulated.
Six straight drive splines form a sliding noncircular coupling in this study. Production spline count, tooth form, helix and fit are not established by the exploded drawing.

Ford family service text identifies the positive brush connector at M and its frame grommet. J&N photographs and Wagner cross-references support a two-feed/two-ground PMGR comparison; this is not a recovered1994F150 brush wiring drawing.

Brushes1and4 are assigned feed and2and3 ground only for this provisional90degree CAD layout. Actual production brush angle, polarity clocking, lead gauge, braid length, joining process and eyelet orientation remain unverified.
Conductors and sleeves are aggregate geometry, not strands or current/thermal/insulation calculations. Flexible braid deformation and brush-wear travel are not modeled.
Commutator-to-armature winding connections, individual winding topology, battery cable and control harness remain open. Complete starter electrical continuity is not claimed.

unresolved: Factory PMGR architecture/counts and manual F2TZ11002ARM identity are supported; J&N replacement cross-reference supplies ten pinion teeth,27.7mm OD and11mm mounting-hole diameter. Remaining dimensions are provisional.
Starter center distance, clocking, axial station,12mm travel and housing envelope are fit-study assumptions. No bellhousing, index-plate bore or mounting bolt support is reconstructed or claimed.

The9.525mm ring-face setback is a manual164-tooth Ford V8 comparison, not a verified4.9L mounting datum. Existing flywheel tooth module/pressure angle are also assumptions; sampled mesh is not production certification.

Internal12/18/48 tooth reducer counts,5:1 ratio, winding/commutator subdivision and clearances are assumptions. Electromagnetics, current, insulation performance, overrunning-clutch internals and solenoid contact switching are not simulated.
Six straight drive splines form a sliding noncircular coupling in this study. Production spline count, tooth form, helix and fit are not established by the exploded drawing.
Factory drawing supports a fork lever and drive assembly, not these arm lengths, groove or slotted-clevis dimensions. All linkage detail and travel are provisional engineering geometry.

A 30mm upper arm and32mm lower arm connect11.25mm solenoid stroke to12mm pinion travel. A transverse slot in the plunger clevis accommodates the upper pin arc; this is not a verified production joint design.
Spherical fork pads engage a3mm-wide annular clutch shift groove. Force, compliance, wear, friction, clutch internals, gear-tooth blocking and real starter sequencing are not simulated.
Housing, front-seat and seal clearances are candidate interface modifications only, not production machining guidance. Default viewer remains static/retracted.

Ford family service text identifies the positive brush connector at M and its frame grommet. J&N photographs and Wagner cross-references support a two-feed/two-ground PMGR comparison; this is not a recovered1994F150 brush wiring drawing.

Brushes1and4 are assigned feed and2and3 ground only for this provisional90degree CAD layout. Actual production brush angle, polarity clocking, lead gauge, braid length, joining process and eyelet orientation remain unverified.
Conductors and sleeves are aggregate geometry, not strands or current/thermal/insulation calculations. Flexible braid deformation and brush-wear travel are not modeled.

definitions.name: Cylinder head
definitions.function: Closes the cylinders and carries the valves, intake and exhaust passages and rocker supports. Port and chamber shapes here are provisional.
unresolved: Photograph-informed chamber outline and plug wells remain provisional. Plug datums are shared with the installed study for geometric coherence, not verified production fit. Chamber volume/profile, port routing, coolant passages, casting identity and valve stations remain unverified.
Firing sequence and clockwise distributor sweep follow Ford references. Tower 1 at local +X is an explicit model phase; surveyed cap clocking and absolute ignition timing are unverified.

Ford describes a carbon-impregnated multifilament synthetic-fiber core and heat-resistant rubber insulation. The 7 mm jacket, 2 mm aggregate core and all boot/contact dimensions are illustrative; individual fibers and electrical resistance are not simulated.
Lead lengths, bends, terminal clip construction, seal compression and support arrangement are provisional. These routes are not an installation guide.
Coil bracket geometry, two head mounting bosses and fasteners are a fit study. Four coil screws follow existing provisional core holes, not a verified factory screw count.
Electrical paths and firing order are represented; ignition voltage, dielectric breakdown, spark timing, flexing and thermal behavior are not simulated.

Ford identifies a shared power-steering/A/C bracket attached to block and head and a separate alternator bracket. These castings reconstruct that load-path topology, not a measured production casting.

All boss coordinates, bolt counts, web sections, material colors, hole sizes and mounting-face locations are illustrative interfaces to the current component studies. Casting ribs, part numbers, dowels and factory contours remain unknown.

Engine feet touch provisional front-face seats. Explicit interface adapters add isolated blind support bosses and 16 mm deep smooth thread-envelope bores; 14 mm bolt engagement is illustrative, not a verified thread specification. These are dry blind attachments, not coolant or oil passages.
Accessory bolt shanks use clearance through the candidate mounting ears. Threads, grades, preload, bracket stiffness and belt-load deflection are not simulated.
The Thermactor and tensioner engine brackets remain separate unresolved load paths. No unsupported air-pump attachment is added to these castings.

All station coordinates, lug sections, eye outline, socket depths and clearances are provisional adaptations to current castings, not production dimensions.

Smooth nominal thread envelopes do not simulate thread engagement, preload, lifting strength or fatigue. The projecting stud end has no invented downstream retaining nut.

The provisional bolt axes are above the intake gasket strip. The casting webs lie outside its sealing plane instead of cutting the gasket into disconnected pieces.

occurrences.name: Camshaft
occurrences.function: Twelve lobes time the intake and exhaust valves. Four bearing journals locate the shaft; the timing gears turn it once per two crankshaft revolutions.

occurrences.name: Camshaft bearing
occurrences.function: Supports a camshaft journal in the block. Inside diameter uses the factory-range midpoint; shell thickness, width, axial stations and oil-feed holes remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Camshaft thrust plate
occurrences.function: Fixed to the block, this plate limits axial camshaft movement between the shaft shoulder and timing-gear hub.

occurrences.name: Cam timing-gear spacer
occurrences.function: Sets the shoulder-to-hub distance around the thrust plate, allowing controlled axial clearance rather than clamping the plate rigidly.

occurrences.name: Camshaft timing-gear key
occurrences.function: Registers the gear to the cam nose through matching shaft and hub seats. The woodruff-form dimensions remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Cam thrust-plate washer
occurrences.function: Separate washer shown under each retaining bolt in the industrial exploded drawing; its section is provisional.

occurrences.name: Cam thrust-plate bolt
occurrences.function: Fastens the stationary thrust plate to the block. The industrial comparison specifies5/16-18 ×3/4-inch.

occurrences.name: Crank Timing Gear
occurrences.function: The direct gear mesh maintains a 2:1 crank-to-cam speed ratio. These are 20-degree involute teaching gears; tooth count and pitch are not verified for the truck.

occurrences.name: Cam Timing Gear
occurrences.function: The direct gear mesh maintains a 2:1 crank-to-cam speed ratio. These are 20-degree involute teaching gears; tooth count and pitch are not verified for the truck.

occurrences.name: Timing cover
occurrences.function: Encloses the gear drive and carries the front crankshaft seal. Casting profile, mounting pattern and water-pump interface remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Front crankshaft seal
occurrences.function: Seals around the rotating front crankshaft snout. The lip is represented by a simple annular solid.

occurrences.name: Rear crankshaft seal
occurrences.function: Limits oil leakage at the rear crankshaft exit. Seal lip and housing fit need exact dimensions.

occurrences.name: Oil pan
occurrences.function: Stores returning oil in a deeper rear sump. The forward section clears the crankcase region; transition and flange geometry remain provisional. Drain dimensions beyond the published thread, sealing details and the pickup-to-floor interface remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Pan drain plug · M14×1.5 comparison
occurrences.function: Closes the replacement-pan drain. Nominal thread diameter and pitch follow Dorman264-011; head size, length, tolerance and location remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Pan drain sealing washer
occurrences.function: Seals the plug shoulder against the modeled flat seating patch. Washer dimensions, material and installed compression are unverified.

occurrences.name: Valve cover
occurrences.function: Contains oil around the rocker gear. Sloped shoulders and separate oil-fill/ventilation openings replace the box envelope. Exact stamping contours, mounting holes, baffles and opening stations remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Valve cover gasket
occurrences.function: Seals the rocker cover to the head. Bolt-hole pattern and corner radii are pending.

occurrences.name: Oil filler cap
occurrences.function: Closes the oil-fill opening in the valve cover. Retention features are provisional.

occurrences.name: Lower EFI intake manifold
occurrences.function: Connects the six upper runners to the cylinder-head intake ports. The truck parts catalog lists E7TZ9424D. Internal passages are open in this study, but production port and injector-socket dimensions remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Intake-to-head gasket
occurrences.function: Seals the six lower-manifold intake interfaces at the cylinder head. This provisional connected-pad layout omits the exact bolt pattern and production gasket contour.

occurrences.name: Upper-to-lower intake gasket
occurrences.function: Seals the joint between the two intake castings. A leak at this joint can admit unmetered air. The gasket remains a dimensional study, not a traced production outline.

occurrences.name: Upper EFI intake manifold
occurrences.function: A common plenum distributes air into six curved runners feeding the lower manifold. The catalog lists E7TZ9424A. This is one casting, not six removable runner tubes. The throttle-body interface is open; a separate throttle mechanism mounts at this interface.

occurrences.name: Cylinder 1 · coil
occurrences.function: Current from the engine controller creates a magnetic field that lifts the armature. Shown as a winding envelope, not individual copper turns.

occurrences.name: Cylinder 1 · inlet filter
occurrences.function: Screens fuel entering from the rail. The cup illustrates the integral filter; actual mesh and flow resistance are unresolved.

occurrences.name: Cylinder 1 · return spring

occurrences.name: Cylinder 1 · seat
occurrences.function: Provides the closing surface around the outlet. The simple circular opening is not the calibrated production orifice.

occurrences.name: Cylinder 1 · protection cap

occurrences.name: Spark-plug center electrode · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: The firing end faces the ground strap across the specified application gap. Electrode construction is illustrative.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug electrode core · illustrative · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: Illustrates a separate heat-conducting electrode core; WR4-1 internal dimensions remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug suppressor resistor · illustrative · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: Represents the internal interference-suppression element; resistance and construction are not specified by this model.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug lower conductive seal · illustrative · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: Illustrates an internal conducting seal between electrode and resistor.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug upper conductive seal · illustrative · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: Illustrates an internal conducting seal between resistor and terminal stem.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug terminal and stem · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: Receives the plug-wire connection and carries voltage toward the internal resistor.

occurrences.name: Spark-plug ground electrode · cylinder 6
occurrences.function: The ground strap returns spark current through the shell to the cylinder head. Its gap is modeled at .044 inch.

occurrences.name: PCV metal valve body
occurrences.function: Houses the metering mechanism and inserts into the cover grommet. The external shoulder follows the replacement photo; rolled seams and production dimensions are unresolved.

occurrences.name: PCV angled outlet head
occurrences.function: Connects the valve passage to two perpendicular hose outlets, following the V219 replacement exterior. Which outlet is used or closed on this truck remains unverified.

occurrences.name: PCV metering plunger
occurrences.function: Moves under the balance of pressure and spring force to change the flow opening. The factory describes metering and preventing backfire propagation; this pose has no calibrated flow or motion.

occurrences.name: PCV orifice washer
occurrences.function: Provides the metering opening around the tapered plunger. Factory cutaway establishes this separate element; its bore and profile are provisional.

occurrences.name: PCV metering spring
occurrences.function: Loads the plunger against pressure forces. Wire diameter, coil count, spring rate and preload are illustrative.

occurrences.name: PCV mounting grommet
occurrences.function: Locates and seals the valve at the cover opening. Ford calls for inspecting this separate grommet for deterioration. The lips fit the provisional cover opening without modeled rubber compression.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch metal body
occurrences.function: Admits oil through the inlet and provides the grounded housing. The inlet thread is a nominal envelope with unverified dimensions.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch diaphragm
occurrences.function: Separates oil from the electrical chamber and transmits pressure force. Manufacturer material description supports a diaphragm; this flat pose does not simulate deformation.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch contact carrier
occurrences.function: Illustrative insulated carrier transfers diaphragm displacement to the moving contact. Internal construction is not established by the exterior photograph.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch moving contact
occurrences.function: In this illustrative normally-open arrangement, upward displacement meets the fixed contact and grounds the terminal. The factory EVTM establishes the switching behavior, not this contact shape.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch terminal and fixed contact
occurrences.function: Connects the external single stud to the fixed contact. Contact flange and stud dimensions are provisional.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch terminal insulator
occurrences.function: Insulates the terminal from the grounded metal housing. Blue exterior follows the manufacturer photograph.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch retaining rim
occurrences.function: Illustrates the metal crimp retaining the insulating cap. Manufacturing seam and forming details remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch return spring
occurrences.function: Illustrative spring opposes pressure force and returns the contacts to their open state. No threshold or spring rate is assigned.

occurrences.name: Pressure switch ground contact bridge
occurrences.function: Illustrates the electrical connection from the moving contact to the grounded body. Its flexible construction is hypothetical, not a documented production part.

occurrences.name: Rear camshaft bore plug
occurrences.function: Closes the rear access opening of the camshaft tunnel. The cup is a separate stationary seal; it does not support or retain the rotating camshaft.

occurrences.name: EGR valve body
occurrences.function: Routes exhaust through a pintle-controlled seat to the intake outlet.

occurrences.name: EGR pintle guide
occurrences.function: Guides the sliding stem between the hot passage and diaphragm chamber. Seal construction remains unresolved.

occurrences.name: EGR pintle and stem
occurrences.function: Lifts away from the seat as the vacuum diaphragm moves, admitting exhaust into the intake passage.

occurrences.name: EGR lower diaphragm housing
occurrences.function: Supports the diaphragm and provides the atmospheric side of its pressure difference.

occurrences.name: EGR diaphragm
occurrences.function: Converts the pressure difference across the flexible membrane into stem motion.

occurrences.name: EGR lower diaphragm support plate
occurrences.function: Supports the diaphragm around its center; the production reinforcement and attachment remain provisional.

occurrences.name: EGR upper diaphragm support plate
occurrences.function: Transfers load between the diaphragm and pintle attachment.

occurrences.name: EGR stem retainer
occurrences.function: Illustrates the center attachment; its actual staking or fastening process is not established.

occurrences.name: EGR closing spring
occurrences.function: Biases the valve closed when the vacuum command is removed. Spring rate and preload are unverified.

occurrences.name: EGR closing-spring seat
occurrences.function: Illustrative separate seat supporting the spring above the diaphragm center.

occurrences.name: EGR vacuum chamber cover
occurrences.function: Encloses the vacuum side of the diaphragm, with passages for the vacuum nipple and EVP follower.

occurrences.name: EGR vacuum nipple
occurrences.function: Connects the chamber to the regulator-controlled vacuum hose. Tube size is assumed.

occurrences.name: EGR intake gasket
occurrences.function: Seals the valve outlet to the upper intake. This fit-study contour has one functional passage; the replacement kit photograph includes a two-port gasket whose second opening is not yet reconciled.

occurrences.name: EGR mounting bolt
occurrences.function: One of two fasteners retaining the valve. Size, thread, washer arrangement and torque remain unverified.

occurrences.name: EGR mounting bolt
occurrences.function: One of two fasteners retaining the valve. Size, thread, washer arrangement and torque remain unverified.

occurrences.name: EVP sensor housing
occurrences.function: Supports the follower, electrical contact study and three-terminal connector. The exact internal molding is not established.

occurrences.name: EVP sensor lid

occurrences.name: EVP flange seal
occurrences.function: Illustrates the separate circular seal shown with the replacement valve. Profile and compression are unverified.

occurrences.name: EVP spring-loaded follower
occurrences.function: Follows the valve stem to provide a displacement input to the position sensor.

occurrences.name: EVP follower spring
occurrences.function: Keeps the illustrative follower in contact with the valve. Rate and installed preload are not established.

occurrences.name: EVP spring stop
occurrences.function: Illustrative fixed stop above the follower spring; production support construction remains unresolved.

occurrences.name: EVP resistive-element carrier

occurrences.name: EVP resistance track
occurrences.function: Represents the potentiometer resistance between reference voltage and signal return. Physical track shape and resistance are unverified.

occurrences.name: EVP signal collector
occurrences.function: Illustrative sliding-contact collector for the sensor output; the EVTM establishes three-terminal topology, not this contact layout.

occurrences.name: EVP wiper contact
occurrences.function: Bridges the resistance track and output collector in this teaching layout. Displacement changes the sampled potential.

occurrences.function: Joins the tube to the rear exhaust collector. The hollow fitting and collector bore share a gas passage; thread and sealing details remain unverified.

occurrences.name: EVR upper cap

occurrences.name: Damper hub
occurrences.function: Connects the damper assembly to the crankshaft. The modeled keyway and retaining joint illustrate the attachment; production dimensions remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Damper elastomer
occurrences.function: An elastic layer couples the hub to the inertia ring; deformation dissipates torsional vibration energy. This section is illustrative.

occurrences.name: Damper inertia ring
occurrences.function: The outer mass responds to crankshaft torsional oscillation through the elastic coupling. Rigid viewer rotation does not simulate vibration or damping.

occurrences.name: Crankshaft damper key
occurrences.function: Locates the damper angularly on the crankshaft. The rectangular key and its pockets illustrate the joint; actual key shape and dimensions remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Damper retaining washer
occurrences.function: Spreads the center-bolt clamping load onto the damper hub face. Diameter and thickness are provisional.

occurrences.name: Damper retaining bolt
occurrences.function: Clamps the damper against its crankshaft seat. The smooth shank illustrates the fastener; thread, grade and installed engagement remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Fuel regulator vacuum hose
occurrences.function: Connects the regulator spring chamber to intake manifold pressure so fuel pressure is referenced to the injector outlet pressure. The route is provisional.

occurrences.name: Regulator manifold vacuum fitting · provisional
occurrences.function: Provides an open connection through the modeled plenum wall. A dedicated fitting is a construction assumption; the production vacuum harness and port identity remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Heater supply and ECT elbow
occurrences.function: Connects the thermostat-side coolant passage to the engine-side heater supply endpoint and exposes the ECT probe to coolant. Bend shape and all dimensions are provisional.

occurrences.name: Heater return tube at water pump
occurrences.function: Returns heater coolant through an opened passage into the existing pump chamber. The open upper end is a vehicle-interface endpoint, not an installed hose.

occurrences.name: ECT sensor metal body
occurrences.function: Conducts coolant temperature to an internal NTC thermistor. Ford specifies a two-lead ECT with 3/8-18 NPTF-SPL dry-seal thread; the modeled thread envelope and probe dimensions are illustrative.

occurrences.name: ECT sensor connector insulator
occurrences.function: Separates the two terminals from the metal sensor body. Connector shape, keying and sealing details remain provisional.

occurrences.name: ECT sensing thermistor · envelope
occurrences.function: Decreases resistance as coolant temperature rises, changing the PCM input. Shape, encapsulation and thermal interface are illustrative.

occurrences.name: ECT terminal and internal lead
occurrences.function: One of two independent conductors: ECT signal and sensor return. This sensor does not use its body as the circuit return; exact connector geometry is unresolved.

occurrences.name: ECT terminal and internal lead
occurrences.function: One of two independent conductors: ECT signal and sensor return. This sensor does not use its body as the circuit return; exact connector geometry is unresolved.

occurrences.name: Tensioner pulley wheel
occurrences.function: The smooth steel surface contacts the back of the accessory belt. The rim and web are one illustrative wheel; a separate support study carries the bearing, while the belt and engine bracket remain missing.

occurrences.name: Tensioner pulley bearing · unresolved cartridge
occurrences.function: Allows the pulley wheel to turn around its stationary mounting axis. Only the 17 mm bore is sourced; the outer envelope and internal construction remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Tensioner spring/pivot cartridge · unresolved interior
occurrences.function: Houses the enclosed preloaded spring that biases the arm. This envelope intentionally leaves spring turns, anchors, damping and stops unresolved; the rear locating pin registers the housing.

occurrences.name: Tensioner moving arm
occurrences.function: Carries the pulley bearing on an offset journal and transfers belt load to the spring pivot. Its simplified contour, journal and working angle are provisional.

occurrences.name: Tensioner pivot sleeve · illustrative
occurrences.function: Illustrates separation of arm rotation from the central mounting fastener. The actual bearing or bushing arrangement has not been sourced.

occurrences.name: Tensioner central mounting bolt · illustrative
occurrences.function: Represents the central attachment described by Gates. The supporting engine bracket, thread and clamping stack still require evidence.

occurrences.name: Tensioner pulley retaining bolt · illustrative
occurrences.function: Illustrates retention on the arm journal. Fastener dimensions, thread and contact with the unresolved bearing cartridge are assumptions; separate bearing races are not reconstructed.

occurrences.name: Tensioner locating-pin bushing · optional
occurrences.function: Adapts the rear locating pin to the larger bracket-hole variant described in the Gates 38131 instructions. The installed bracket option is unknown.

occurrences.name: Alternator drive housing
occurrences.function: Supports the pulley-side bearing and two mounting ears. Vent, ear and bearing-seat geometry is illustrative; engine bracket remains unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator rear housing
occurrences.function: Supports the rear bearing and encloses the rectifier. Openings and bolt pattern are provisional.

occurrences.name: Alternator stator iron core
occurrences.function: Provides the magnetic path around the rotating claw poles. Laminations and slot geometry are not individually reconstructed.

occurrences.name: Alternator stator winding envelope
occurrences.function: Stationary windings produce AC as rotor poles pass. Copper-colored volume shows the active winding and end-turn regions without claiming exact wire paths or turns.

occurrences.name: Alternator rotor front claw pole
occurrences.function: Interleaves with the opposite pole around the field coil. Six illustrative fingers per half are not a verified Ford pole count.

occurrences.name: Alternator rotor rear claw pole and core
occurrences.function: Carries the field-coil core and opposing magnetic fingers. The combined core and pole are an illustrative magnetic construction.

occurrences.name: Alternator rotor field-coil envelope
occurrences.function: Field current magnetizes the rotor pole pieces. This is a coil-volume envelope; winding turns and leads remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator rotor shaft
occurrences.function: Carries the pulley, rotor and slip rings. Diameters, shoulders, press fits and end threads remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Alternator front bearing cartridge
occurrences.function: Supports the pulley side of the rotor. Races, rolling elements, seals and production bearing identity remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator rear bearing cartridge
occurrences.function: Supports the rear of the rotor shaft. Internal bearing construction and fit are not reconstructed.

occurrences.name: Alternator external cooling fan · provisional
occurrences.function: Illustrates conventional-alternator cooling airflow through housing vents. External versus internal fan variant and blade geometry remain unverified for the installed unit.

occurrences.name: Alternator pulley spacer · illustrative
occurrences.function: Separates pulley and fan in the study stack. Production spacer identity and clamping stack remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator six-groove pulley · provisional
occurrences.function: Transfers accessory-belt torque to the rotor. The 70 mm diameter, six-groove profile and ratio are illustrative; the belt plane is shared only as a modeling datum.

occurrences.name: Alternator pulley nut · illustrative
occurrences.function: Represents axial retention of the pulley stack. Thread and torque specification are not modeled.

occurrences.name: Alternator slip-ring insulating sleeve
occurrences.function: Separates the rotating field-current contacts from the shaft. Geometry and electrical clearance are illustrative.

occurrences.name: Alternator brush holder · illustrative
occurrences.function: Locates two stationary brushes at the slip rings. Brush springs, guides and fixing screws remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator regulator · unresolved electronics
occurrences.function: Controls rotor field current to regulate charging voltage. Package is an envelope, without invented circuitry or connector pin placement.

occurrences.name: Alternator rectifier · unresolved electronics
occurrences.function: Converts stator AC to DC. Annular volume locates the assembly; semiconductor count, heat sink, insulation and terminals remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Alternator slip ring 1
occurrences.function: Provides a rotating contact for rotor field current. Ring section and electrical connections are illustrative.

occurrences.name: Alternator brush 1

occurrences.name: Alternator slip ring 2

occurrences.name: Alternator brush 2

occurrences.name: Pump housing and front plate

occurrences.name: Reinforced-nylon reservoir and return nipple
occurrences.function: Stores steering fluid around the pump housing. Owner photographs show a yellowed translucent reservoir and dark cap; hollow body, filler neck and return passage have provisional contour and thickness.

occurrences.name: Shaft support bushing · illustrative

occurrences.name: Pump shaft seal
occurrences.function: Separates the fluid cavity from the rotating drive shaft. The lip profile and material stack are unresolved.

occurrences.name: Shaft seal retainer
occurrences.function: Represents the seal retainer shown in the Ford exploded drawing. Exact section and retention fit are provisional.

occurrences.name: Pressure-plate disc spring
occurrences.function: Preloads the pressure-plate stack. Ford specifies its dished orientation; modeled deflection and spring rate are illustrative.

occurrences.name: Lower pressure plate

occurrences.name: Lower pressure-plate outer seal

occurrences.name: Lower pressure-plate inner seal

occurrences.name: CII slipper-pump cam ring

occurrences.name: CII ten-pocket rotor
occurrences.function: Carries ten spring-loaded slippers, as specified by the Ford assembly procedure. Pocket contour and shaft interface remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Rotor shaft retaining clip

occurrences.name: Upper pressure plate

occurrences.name: Pump valve cover

occurrences.name: Filter element tension clip

occurrences.name: FS10 Rear Cylinder

occurrences.name: FS10 Rear Suction Reed

occurrences.name: FS10 Rear Discharge Reed

occurrences.name: FS10 Clutch Pulley

occurrences.name: FS10 discharge port O-ring · size 211 comparison

occurrences.name: Starter armature thrust ball
occurrences.function: Separate thrust ball identified by Ford between the armature and output-shaft region. It provides a localized axial interface; Hertzian stress and lubrication are not calculated.

occurrences.name: Starter gear retainer
occurrences.function: Retains the planetary components axially on the armature side. Its profile and clearances are provisional rather than a traced Ford retainer drawing.

occurrences.name: Starter stationary gear
occurrences.function: Fixed internal ring gear reacting the planet forces into the housing. With the assumed 12-tooth sun and 48-tooth ring fixed, the output carrier rotates at one fifth of sun speed.

occurrences.name: Starter planet gear 1
occurrences.function: One of three planet gears meshing with the sun and fixed internal ring. Each spins on a carrier pin while its center orbits the sun. The displayed 18-tooth count is provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter planet gear 2
occurrences.function: One of three planet gears meshing with the sun and fixed internal ring. Each spins on a carrier pin while its center orbits the sun. The displayed 18-tooth count is provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter planet gear 3
occurrences.function: One of three planet gears meshing with the sun and fixed internal ring. Each spins on a carrier pin while its center orbits the sun. The displayed 18-tooth count is provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter output shaft assembly
occurrences.function: Integral carrier, three planet pins and output shaft collect the reduced-speed drive. Six provisional straight splines form a sliding noncircular coupling to the drive-clutch sleeve.

occurrences.name: Starter armature thrust washer
occurrences.function: Provides a separate axial spacing and thrust surface in the drive-shaft stack. The washer is not a substitute for the overrunning clutch.

occurrences.name: Starter shaft e ring
occurrences.function: Separate open retaining ring locating the shaft stack axially. Groove geometry, snap fit and retention capacity remain unverified.

occurrences.name: Starter drive clutch
occurrences.function: Sliding clutch envelope with a provisional annular shift groove engaged by the fork pads. The sleeve retains its noncircular shaft coupling throughout12mm travel. Overrunning clutch internals and loaded operation remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter drive pinion
occurrences.function: Ten-tooth pinion translates12mm with the clutch during the prescribed linkage stroke. Its sourced27.7mm outside diameter and provisional manual-flywheel mounting datums are unchanged.

occurrences.name: Starter stop ring
occurrences.function: Locates the forward travel-stop region on the output shaft. Exact groove dimensions and engagement travel require an applicable production reference.

occurrences.name: Starter stop ring retainer
occurrences.function: Retains the drive stop ring as a separate component. The stop stack is distinct from the pinion, clutch and nose bushing.

occurrences.name: Starter drive lever
occurrences.function: Rigid fork lever pivots about the fixed fulcrum. Its upper pin slides in the translating plunger clevis, while integral spherical lower pads retain axial contact with the clutch shift groove. Dimensions and joint construction are provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid clevis pin
occurrences.function: Captured pivot pin follows the upper lever arc and slides transversely within the plunger clevis. End shoulders prevent axial escape in this provisional joint; load and wear are not calculated.

occurrences.name: Starter lever pivot
occurrences.function: Provides the fulcrum for the drive lever within the drive-end housing. Pivot fit and bearing pressure are provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter housing seal
occurrences.function: Separate seal envelope with a provisional enlarged slot clearing the rotating lever stem. Elastomer deformation, environmental sealing and production dimensions remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid shell
occurrences.function: Encloses the solenoid and provides the provisional hold-winding ground attachment. The attachment is a packaging study rather than a verified Ford joint construction.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid plunger
occurrences.function: Translating magnetic plunger with a provisional transverse-slot clevis. The slot accommodates the lever pin arc during the11.25mm prescribed stroke without forcing the plunger off axis.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid return spring
occurrences.function: Returns the plunger toward the resting position when electromagnetic force is removed. The spring geometry has no calibrated force or release-time claim.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid B battery terminal
occurrences.function: Heavy power terminal with an internal fixed contact face. B/M assignment is the candidate convention; clocking and internal geometry are provisional.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid terminal nut 1
occurrences.function: Retains a cable lug on a large solenoid terminal. No cable lug is installed here, and the smooth bore is not a modeled screw thread.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid M motor terminal
occurrences.function: Heavy M terminal joins the pull-winding end and external positive-brush connector. The power-contact bridge supplies M at closure. Armature winding connections and complete electrical performance remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid terminal nut 2
occurrences.function: Retains a cable lug on a large solenoid terminal. No cable lug is installed here, and the smooth bore is not a modeled screw thread.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid screw 1
occurrences.function: Fastens the solenoid front mounting ears to the drive-end housing. Matching holes provide a visible attachment without a calibrated clamp-load claim.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid screw 2
occurrences.function: Fastens the solenoid front mounting ears to the drive-end housing. Matching holes provide a visible attachment without a calibrated clamp-load claim.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid end cap
occurrences.function: Insulating end-cap envelope surrounding the terminal penetrations. It is separate from the metal shell; contact switching and dielectric performance are unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid front seat
occurrences.function: Mounting seat with a provisional13mm-radius aperture clearing the lever stem and slotted clevis throughout the prescribed stroke. Its ears still attach to the drive housing.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid pull winding
occurrences.function: Aggregate insulated pull winding between S and M. Two provisional coil-end conductors attach it to those terminals; individual winding turns and resistance remain unresolved. Closing the B/M bridge shunts this winding in the declared circuit.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid hold winding
occurrences.function: Aggregate insulated hold winding between S and frame. Two provisional coil-end conductors attach it to S and the shell; magnetic force, winding turns and resistance remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid winding bobbin
occurrences.function: Provisional insulating former and divider with four bored lead passages. Separate sleeves clear the passage walls; dimensions and production lead routing are unverified.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid fixed pole
occurrences.function: Provisional stationary magnetic pole with four insulated lead feedthroughs around the contact pushrod guide. Magnetic flux and production pole construction are not solved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid contact rod
occurrences.function: Provisional rod translating with the plunger to carry the insulated moving contact. Its connection to the existing plunger is a geometric study.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid bridge insulator
occurrences.function: Insulating sleeve and axial shoulders isolate the moving power-contact bridge from its steel rod.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid contact bridge
occurrences.function: Normally open copper bridge connecting the B and M contact faces at the candidate stroke endpoint. This is a physical contact study, not a current-carrying certification.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid s terminal
occurrences.function: Small S control terminal joined to both provisional coil-start conductors. Its external control harness remains absent; terminal clocking and joint construction are assumed.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid s terminal insulator
occurrences.function: Insulating sleeve through the contact-cap wall for the distinct S terminal. Material and dielectric performance are unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead pull s
occurrences.function: Provisional coil-end conductor with nonpenetrating winding and terminal/frame attachment faces. The two S conductors contact separate patches of the same terminal; aggregate winding interiors remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead insulation pull s
occurrences.function: Separate provisional dielectric sleeve around one coil-end conductor. The two S sleeves remain physically separated; the S sleeve ends meet the existing terminal insulator without overlapping material.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead pull m
occurrences.function: Provisional coil-end conductor with nonpenetrating winding and terminal/frame attachment faces. The two S conductors contact separate patches of the same terminal; aggregate winding interiors remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead insulation pull m
occurrences.function: Separate provisional dielectric sleeve around one coil-end conductor. The two S sleeves remain physically separated; the S sleeve ends meet the existing terminal insulator without overlapping material.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead hold s
occurrences.function: Provisional coil-end conductor with nonpenetrating winding and terminal/frame attachment faces. The two S conductors contact separate patches of the same terminal; aggregate winding interiors remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead insulation hold s
occurrences.function: Separate provisional dielectric sleeve around one coil-end conductor. The two S sleeves remain physically separated; the S sleeve ends meet the existing terminal insulator without overlapping material.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead hold frame
occurrences.function: Provisional coil-end conductor with nonpenetrating winding and terminal/frame attachment faces. The two S conductors contact separate patches of the same terminal; aggregate winding interiors remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter solenoid lead insulation hold frame
occurrences.function: Separate provisional dielectric sleeve around one coil-end conductor. The two S sleeves remain physically separated; the S sleeve ends meet the existing terminal insulator without overlapping material.

occurrences.name: Starter motor positive feed
occurrences.function: Provisional common positive conductor and eyelet join solenoid M to two brush pigtails. Ford PMGR-family service text establishes this connector role; braid geometry and installed routing are assumed.

occurrences.name: Starter motor feed jacket
occurrences.function: Separate provisional dielectric jacket surrounds the external motor-feed conductor. It meets a separate frame grommet; material, thickness and electrical durability are unverified.

occurrences.name: Starter motor feed grommet
occurrences.function: Flanged provisional insulating grommet locates the motor feed through the bored frame wall. It represents the grommet identified by Ford, without claiming production shape or environmental sealing.

occurrences.name: Starter motor ground bridge
occurrences.function: Common provisional metal return bridge connects two ground pigtails to the rear end plate and retaining screws. A metal ground bracket is visible in comparison photographs; this annular profile and two-pad construction are assumed.

occurrences.name: Starter brush pigtail positive 1
occurrences.function: Separate provisional flexible braid envelope joins one brush to its feed or return conductor at nonpenetrating attachment faces. Strand construction, brush-wear travel and lead deformation remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter brush pigtail positive 4
occurrences.function: Separate provisional flexible braid envelope joins one brush to its feed or return conductor at nonpenetrating attachment faces. Strand construction, brush-wear travel and lead deformation remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter brush pigtail ground 2
occurrences.function: Separate provisional flexible braid envelope joins one brush to its feed or return conductor at nonpenetrating attachment faces. Strand construction, brush-wear travel and lead deformation remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Starter brush pigtail ground 3
occurrences.function: Separate provisional flexible braid envelope joins one brush to its feed or return conductor at nonpenetrating attachment faces. Strand construction, brush-wear travel and lead deformation remain unresolved.

occurrences.name: Front Manifold Lifting Eye
occurrences.function: Spans two separate front-manifold mounting regions; each foot is clamped against a casting lug. This geometric load path does not establish a safe lifting rating.

occurrences.name: Front Manifold Stud13
occurrences.function: Its integral shoulder clamps one eye foot and the front casting against the head. The external extension represents the compared long stud, not a completed downstream attachment.

occurrences.name: Front Manifold Bolt14
occurrences.function: Clamps the second eye foot and front casting into a separate blind head socket before the intake is installed.

occurrences.name: Intake manifold locating dowel
occurrences.function: Locates the intake gasket and lower manifold relative to the cylinder head. It enters separate blind sockets; it is not a substitute for the missing manifold clamp fasteners.

occurrences.name: Rear Manifold Bolt15
occurrences.function: Clamps a rear manifold mounting land to a blind head socket before intake installation; geometry and retention remain provisional.

occurrences.name: Rear Manifold Bolt16

dorman-674186-head-facing-photo.title: Dorman 674-186 head-facing manufacturer photograph
dorman-674186-head-facing-photo.application: Viewed: three rectangular entries and irregular separate lands. No dimensions inferred from pixels.

dorman-674186-opposite-photo.title: Dorman 674-186 opposite-side manufacturer photograph
dorman-674186-opposite-photo.application: Viewed: outlet flange and auxiliary plugged bosses near discharge. Port functions and installed orientation require additional evidence.

dorman-674186-overview-photo.title: Dorman 674-186 manufacturer overview photograph
dorman-674186-overview-photo.application: Viewed replacement assembly; loose package hardware does not establish cylinder-head fastener topology.

dorman-674186-catalog-application.title: Dorman 2006 catalog: F-100/150 rear manifold application, PDF130 / printed128
dorman-674186-catalog-application.application: Manufacturer catalog on public mirror; visually reviewed F-100/150 4.9L 1994-90 row lists 674-186 RH/Rear. Replacement applicability, not installed identity.

dorman-674185-profile-specification.title: Dorman674-185 front manifold specification and OE cross references
dorman-674185-profile-specification.application: Manufacturer states rectangular ports and cast iron, with F5TZ9430-A/F cross references. No dimensional drawing or installed truck identity.

dorman-674185-head-facing-photo.title: Dorman674-185 head-facing photograph
dorman-674185-head-facing-photo.application: Three rounded-rectangular entries, individual flange pads and two enclosed end-wing holes are visible. Image not scaled into manufacturing dimensions.

dorman-674185-opposite-photo.title: Dorman674-185 opposite-side photograph
dorman-674185-opposite-photo.application: Blended branches and round outlet with two-hole flange are visible. Outlet mounting detail is not completed by the current study.

dorman-674185-application.title: Dorman674-185 manufacturer vehicle application table
dorman-674185-application.application: Explicit1994 Ford F150 L6 300 4.9L front replacement application. Not evidence that this aftermarket part is installed on the truck.

ford-intake-manifold-dowel.title: Ford1994 4.9L intake locating-dowel installation
ford-intake-manifold-dowel.application: Applicable factory text specifies one locating dowel for the intake gasket and lower intake. Diameter, length, station and fits are not dimensioned here.
